# Glowbar, fluxbox and hexmatrix

::: {.doc-lead}
Show observations, summaries and density with individually named plot parts.
:::

Three signature plots show observations beside their summary. Each takes a table (a pandas or polars DataFrame, or a dict of columns) plus column names, seaborn-style, and names every part for you. Hover a real fluxbox on the [semantic plots](/docs/semantic-plots.html#every-part-has-a-name) page to see those names. In the examples, `df` is your table and `ax` an axes.

## Glowbar

```python
gb = fp.glowbar(df, x="condition", y="APP/GAPDH", units="subject", ax=ax)

# Paired or repeated measures: connect each unit across conditions.
gb = fp.glowbar(df, x="condition", y="signal", units="mouse",
                connect_identical_points_across_x_values=True, ax=ax)
```

Every observation is a dot. Beside each group sits a slim bar that *glows* — its ink densest at
the centre of the distribution and fading to hard caps at the interval ends — with the **mean** as
a heavy, haloed line across the bar and the **median** as a V-notch cut into both of its edges.
The interval is mean ± SEM by default, glowing around the mean; `interval="iqr"` spans the box of
a box plot and glows around the median, `"sd"` gives mean ± SD, and a callable
`values -> (low, high)` is accepted. Default groups use ColorBrewer's `YlGnBu`, then `YlOrRd`.

With `units=` every unit (animal, subject, cell) keeps a **fixed lane and colour derived from the
table, never from the values**, so plots of different measures made from one table agree dot for
dot — even when a unit is missing from one of them. Unit colours are equal *perceptual* steps
(CAM02-UCS) of each group's ColorBrewer map between `shade_range=(88, 22)` lightness, dealt across
lanes so neighbours always contrast (`interleave_shades=True`), and rimmed in a deeper shade of
themselves so the palest dots stay crisp (`point_edge="rim"`). Connectors are a quiet neutral grey
and break at a unit's missing category rather than bridging it.

| Part | Role | Default ID |
|---|---|---|
| interval glow | `box` | `<category>.glow` |
| interval caps | `cap` | `<category>.caps` |
| mean line | `mean` | `<category>.mean` |
| median notch | `median` | `<category>.median` |
| a unit's points | `point` | `<unit>.points`, `<unit>.point.<k>` |
| a unit's connector | `line` | `<unit>.line` |
| points without `units` | `point` | `<category>.points`, `<category>.point.<k>` |

Each category series carries a `glowbar` manifest payload with the exact statistics drawn (`n`,
`mean`, `median`, `sd`, `sem`, `q1`, `q3`, `interval`, `low`, `high`, `center`, `x`, `groupColor`),
and each unit series its identity (`units`, `unit`, `categories`, `colors`); the manifest's
`plotType` is `"glowbar"`. Series names default to the category and unit values; `series=` and
`unit_series=` (a mapping or a callable) rename them.

Every visual choice is a keyword (see [`fp.glowbar`](/docs/fluxplot-api.html#glowbar) for all of them):

- **Bar**: `bar_width`, `bar_offset`, `bar_side` (`"outer"`, the default, puts the first
  category's bar left of its points and every other bar to the right; `"left"` or `"right"`
  applies to all), `glow_steps`, `glow_alpha`.
- **Mean, median and caps**: `mean_line_width`, `mean_color`, `mean_halo_width`,
  `median_notch_depth`, `median_notch_height`, `cap_width`, `cap_color`, and the switches
  `show_mean`, `show_median`, `show_caps`, `show_individual_points`.
- **Points**: `point_size`, `jitter`, `point_edge`, `point_fill_alpha` (fill only; the rim stays
  opaque).
- **Colour**: `palette` (per category: any `fp.colors.maps` colormap such as
  `"cmasher.emerald"`, any `fp.colors.palettes` palette such as `"brewer.Set2"` or
  `"tol.bright"`, a matplotlib map, a list of colours or one colour; glowbar picks as many
  distinct point colours as it needs plus a solid group colour), `group_color`,
  `group_color_position`, `point_colors`, `shade_range`, `interleave_shades`.
- **Connectors**: `connect_line_width`, `connect_color`, `connect_alpha`.

It returns a `GlowbarResult` (`.ax`, `.categories`, `.stats`, `.group_colors`, `.point_colors`,
`.series`, `.unit_series`, `.artists`). The fluxplot repository's `examples/glowbar_example.py`
draws both designs shown above (unpaired and paired).

## Fluxbox

The fluxbox is the glowbar with a box plot for its summary — the same call, the same lanes,
colours, connectors and names, so the two can be swapped for one another dot for dot:

```python
fb = fp.fluxbox(df, x="condition", y="APP/GAPDH", units="subject", ax=ax)
```

Beside each group sits a slim box (Q1–Q3), a half-strength wash of the group colour
(`box_alpha=0.5`). The **median** is a solid line across it in the group's own hue — deepened, or on
a dark background lifted, only as far as it takes to differ from the box by `median_contrast=30`
units of perceived lightness, so it reads for any palette and theme; the whiskers (and fliers) share
that colour, so the box is the only wash. The **mean** is a V-notch cut
into both edges of the box — the glowbar's median notch; a mean outside the box (a strongly skewed
group) keeps its mark as the same two V's drawn solid, pointing in at the whisker. The capless
whiskers reach the most extreme observations within `whis` × IQR of the box (`1.5` — Tukey's rule,
exactly `plt.boxplot`'s whiskers), `"range"`, or a `(low, high)` pair of percentiles. Observations
beyond the whiskers are not drawn again as fliers — the points already show them — unless the
points are hidden (`show_fliers="auto"`).

| Part | Role | Default ID |
|---|---|---|
| box (Q1–Q3) | `box` | `<category>.box` |
| whiskers | `whisker` | `<category>.whiskers` |
| whisker caps (`show_caps=True`) | `cap` | `<category>.caps` |
| median line | `median` | `<category>.median` |
| mean notch | `mean` | `<category>.mean` |
| fliers (points hidden) | `flier` | `<category>.fliers` |
| points and connectors | `point`, `line` | as for the glowbar |

Each category series carries a `fluxbox` manifest payload with the exact statistics drawn (`n`,
`mean`, `median`, `sd`, `sem`, `q1`, `q3`, `iqr`, `whis`, `whiskerLow`, `whiskerHigh`, `outliers`,
`x`, `groupColor`); the manifest's `plotType` is `"fluxbox"`.

The box keywords are `whis`, `box_width`, `box_alpha`, `box_offset`, `box_side`,
`median_line_width`, `median_color` (sets the median colour outright), `median_contrast`,
`mean_notch_depth`, `mean_notch_height`, `whisker_width`, `whisker_color`, `cap_size`,
`cap_width`, `cap_color`, `flier_size`, `cut_color`, and the switches `show_mean`, `show_median`,
`show_whiskers`, `show_caps` and `show_fliers`. Every point, colour, connector and naming keyword
is the glowbar's. It returns a `FluxboxResult` with the same fields as a `GlowbarResult`. The
fluxplot repository's `examples/fluxbox_example.py` draws a complete example.

## Hexmatrix

The hexmatrix tiles the plane with regular hexagons, each one a named part. One call covers a
point cloud's density, a 2D gradient of a third variable, and a matrix drawn on a hex lattice:

```python
# Density with marginal histograms, jointplot-style:
hm = fp.hexmatrix(df, x="x", y="y", ax=ax, color="#4CB391", marginals=True)

# Log-log density with an identity line:
hm = fp.hexmatrix(df, x="wake", y="nrem", ax=ax, xscale="log", yscale="log",
                  norm="log", identity_line=True,
                  colorbar_label="Synapses per hexbin")

# Spatial density in 0.15 mm bins:
hm = fp.hexmatrix(df, x="ccf_x", y="ccf_z", ax=ax, aspect="equal", binwidth=0.15,
                  norm="log", colorbar_label="somata / hexbin")

# A gradient of a third variable, C:
hm = fp.hexmatrix(df, x="x", y="y", C="rate", reduce="median", ax=ax,
                  cmap="RdBu_r", center=0)

# A matrix drawn on a hex lattice:
hm = fp.hexmatrix(matrix=weights, ax=ax, gap=0.08)
```

Hexagons are addressed by their lattice position: `row` counts up the y axis and `col` along x, so
`<series>.hex.<row>.<col>` names the same hexagon in every plot with the same `extent` and grid,
whatever the data. They are regular *on the page*. `aspect="auto"` locks the axes' box aspect so a
later layout pass can't squash them, and `aspect="equal"` bins in true data units. Log axes bin in
log space.

The colour can be a count, `stat="density"`/`"probability"`/`"percent"` (optionally `weights=`), or
a `reduce` of `C` (`mean`, `median`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `std`, `count` or a callable). The scale is
set by `cmap`/`color` (a single-hue ramp), `norm` (`linear`/`log`/`sqrt` or any `Normalize`),
`vmin`/`vmax`, `robust` and `center`. Further keywords:

* `mincnt=0` draws the empty hexagons too;
* `sparse=k` draws points instead of hexagons where fewer than `k` observations fall;
* `show_points` overlays every observation;
* `gap`, `edgecolor`, `linewidth` and `orientation="flat"` shape the hexagons;
* `marginals`, `colorbar` and `identity_line` add furniture.

The colormap and colour limits are recipe controls, exactly as for `fp.heatmap`: Flux's
**Colour scales** editor can change them and regenerate the plot.

| Part | Role | Default ID |
|---|---|---|
| all hexagons | `x-hexbin` | `<series>.hexes` |
| one hexagon | `x-hex` | `<series>.hex.<row>.<col>` |
| sparse or overlaid points | `point` | `<series>-points.points`, `<series>-points.point.<k>` |
| identity line | `reference-line` | `reference-line.identity` |
| marginal histograms (own panels) | `bar` | `<series>-x.bar.<k>`, `<series>-y.bar.<k>` |

Each hexagon element also carries `data-row`, `data-column`, `data-x`, `data-y`, `data-count` and
`data-value` attributes.

The series carries a `hexmatrix` manifest payload: the lattice (orientation, radius, aspect,
scales, extent), the statistic, and every hexagon drawn (`row`, `col`, `x`, `y`, `count`, `value`).
It also carries the usual `field` colour payload; the `plotType` is `"hexmatrix"`. The call returns
a `HexMatrixResult` (`.ax`, `.hexes`, `.bins`, `.cmap`, `.norm`, `.colorbar`, `.marginal_axes`,
`.points`, `.hex_id(row, col)`, `.lookup(x, y)`).

Hexagons stay individually addressable up to `vector_limit` (5000 by default; `None` uses the
save's generic threshold of 800 elements). A larger layer is rasterized like any heavy layer,
but its hexagons stay in the manifest; pass `force_vectors=True` to `fp.save` to keep every
hexagon addressable. On axes that share x or y with other panels, `fp.hexmatrix` leaves the box
aspect unlocked, with a warning, rather than distorting the sibling panels. The fluxplot repository's `examples/hexmatrix_example.py`
draws all five variants shown above.
